title: Wrong Show in Rummy: Declaration Rules and Penalty Points
excerpt: What counts as a wrong show in rummy, the usual 80-point penalty, what happens to the other players, and a checklist to use before you declare.
content:
**Short answer:** a wrong show (also called an invalid declaration) happens when a player declares but their 13 cards do not form a valid hand. In most 13-card rummy formats the penalty is **80 points**, the maximum a player can lose in a single round.

This guide explains card-game rules for general knowledge. Online rummy played for money is prohibited in India under the Online Gaming Act, 2025; see our [online gaming laws guide](/blog/online-gaming-laws-in-india-what-players-should-know). 18+ only.

## What Makes a Declaration Valid

A declaration is valid only if all 13 cards are arranged into correct groups and the hand contains:

- at least **two sequences**, and
- at least **one pure sequence** (no joker used as a substitute).

Every other card must be in a valid sequence or set. The full rules are in [how to play 13-card rummy](/blog/how-to-play-13-card-rummy-rules).

## The Most Common Causes of a Wrong Show

| Mistake | Why it is invalid |
|---|---|
| No pure sequence | Every valid hand needs one |
| Only one sequence in total | The hand needs at least two |
| A joker inside the "pure" sequence | A joker used as a substitute makes it impure |
| A set with two cards of the same suit | Sets need different suits |
| A set of 5 or more cards | Sets have at most 4 cards |
| A wrap-around sequence such as K-A-2 | Sequences cannot wrap past the Ace |
| A group of only 2 cards | Every group needs at least 3 cards |
| Declaring by accident | Many apps treat a mis-tap on "declare" as a real declaration |

## Wrong Show Penalty Points

| Format | Usual penalty |
|---|---|
| Points rummy | 80 points |
| Pool rummy (101 or 201) | 80 points added to your total |
| Deals rummy | 80 points |

These are the common conventions. Individual tables and apps can use different values, so check the table rules before you play.

## What Happens to the Other Players

In most online formats, the player who made the wrong show takes the penalty and the round continues for everyone else. At home tables, house rules vary: some groups end the round and redeal. Agree on this before you start.

## A Checklist Before You Declare

- Is there a **pure sequence**, with no joker used as a substitute?
- Is there a **second sequence** (pure or impure)?
- Does every set have **3 or 4 cards of different suits**?
- Are there any **wrap-around sequences** like K-A-2?
- Is every card in a group, apart from the one in the finish slot?

Taking five seconds to check these points prevents the costliest mistake in rummy. For how points are counted in normal rounds, see [rummy points calculation](/blog/rummy-points-calculation).
